# Nutrition Plan Page

← [Hub: skills.md](../skills.md) · Status: **Built (M7 part 1)**; meal logging and food photos come in M7 parts 2 and 3

**Purpose:** the person's weekly customised meal plan with daily macro and micronutrient targets, generated by the LLM, which the person can change. Today's part of it appears on [Plan for Today](plan-for-today.md).

## Features

1. **Weekly meal plan:** breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks for each day.
2. **Daily targets with the reasoning:** calories, protein, carbs and fat, plus key micronutrients. Each target has a one-line reason, e.g. "Iron target raised because of your low haemoglobin report."
3. **Change and rebalance:** swap a meal or mark a day as eating out; the rest of the week adjusts to stay on target, with a preview before anything changes (same as the [Workout Plan](workout-plan.md)).
4. **Meal swaps:** alternatives with similar macros that fit the person's diet type.
5. **Weekly grocery list** generated from the week's plan.
6. **Matched to workouts:** more carbs and protein on heavy training days (from the [Workout Plan](workout-plan.md)), less on rest days.
7. **Adjusts to what was actually eaten:** uses food logs from [Plan for Today](plan-for-today.md); e.g. if protein is often under target, next week's plan makes it easier to hit.

## Plan inputs

Set on [Settings / Profile](settings-profile.md): diet type (vegetarian / eggetarian / non-vegetarian), cuisine preferences, allergies and disliked foods, meals per day, cooking time available. Plus confirmed facts from [Personal Artifacts](personal-artifacts.md).

## As built (M7 part 1)

**Food data.** `foods` holds USDA FoodData Central (ingredients, nutrients per 100 g) and the Indian Nutrient Databank (INDB: Indian dishes, nutrients per serving, because INDB's per-100 g values include cooking water). Dishes get a meal role (breakfast, main, staple, salad, snack, …), a diet (vegetarian / eggetarian / non-vegetarian, from their ingredients) and pass data checks (protein, carbs and fat must add up to the calories; plausible serving sizes). INDB's "piece" labels can't always be trusted (a 350 kcal "cheela" is made from 55 g of dal, two or three home-sized ones), so a dish over 250 kcal a piece is planned in servings instead, and every dish shows what the planned amount is made of (e.g. "Made with about 80 g moong dal, 100 g potato, 15 g oil"). Deep-fried and very rich dishes (more than 55% of calories from fat) aren't planned; 24 common USDA foods (eggs, chicken breast, curd, fruit, nuts, sprouts, …) have plain names and are used as snacks and protein add-ons. Import: [setup.md](../setup.md).

**Daily targets** (`backend/core/nutrition/targets.py`), each with a one-line reason:
- **Calories:** resting energy (Mifflin-St Jeor, from the latest weigh-in, height, age and sex) × everyday activity (from the last two weeks' average steps; light activity if none) + that day's training from the [Workout Plan](workout-plan.md) (about 4 kcal per kg per hour), then the goal: lose fat −20% (at most 600 kcal), lose fat and build muscle −10%, build muscle +10% (at most 300). Never below 1,200 (women) / 1,500 (men) or resting energy.
- **Protein:** 1.6 g/kg for building muscle, strength or fat loss (1.4 endurance, 1.2 otherwise); above a BMI of 30, from the weight at a BMI of 27.
- **Fat** about 27% of calories (at least 0.6 g/kg); **carbs** the rest, so training days get more carbs; **fibre** 14 g per 1,000 kcal.
- **Vitamins and minerals:** recommended daily amounts for age and sex (US Dietary Reference Intakes); sodium is a 2,300 mg limit.
- No weigh-in yet: the page asks for one (the Body weight box) and makes the plan as soon as it's saved.

**Making the week** (`backend/core/nutrition/generate.py`): meals per day from Settings (1: lunch; 2: lunch, dinner; 3: + breakfast; 4: + a snack; 5–6: more snacks), each with a share of the day's calories (breakfast 25%, lunch 32%, dinner 30%, snack 13%). Foods are filtered by diet type, allergies and dislikes (by name and ingredients, with common names, e.g. capsicum = shimla mirch, peanut = groundnut; "None" / "NA" mean nothing). The LLM chooses dishes from candidate lists (a fresh sample each week; last week's mains go to the back; protein-rich first) for variety, cuisines and cooking time; invalid choices fall back to the rules' rotation (no main twice within two days, lunch and dinner differ, plain chapati or rice most days, a salad or raita with lunch). A dish is only a candidate if its smallest portion fits the person's meal (a 400 kcal dosa is too much for a 350 kcal breakfast). The rules then size portions (whole chapatis, eggs and idlis; half bowls and plates) to each meal's share, and add a simple protein (Greek yogurt, tofu, eggs, curd, chicken, chickpeas, …; never meat at breakfast or with a meat dish) where a day falls below 90% of its protein target, only as much as keeps that meal within 20% of its share, noting it on the meal. Checked over 200 random weeks each for three very different people: days land within about 5% of the calorie target (never more than 30% off), with protein at about 85–95% of target. Days already past keep their meals. Vercel first (Groq, 25 s), otherwise the `generate_meal_plan` job on the Mac (Groq → Ollama → rules).

**The page:** the week's rationale, day tabs (today first), targets vs what's planned with bars and "Why these targets?", vitamins and minerals, then the meals (dishes with portions, calories and protein). On your own plan, from today on:
- **Swap dish:** six alternatives in the same role that fit the diet and allergies, closest in protein for their calories; the meal is resized.
- **Eating out:** tick meals, then **Preview the change**: each counts as a meal about 30% richer than planned (an estimate), and the extra is taken from the following days, one meal a day (up to 10% of the day), until it's made up, so the week stays on target; **Use this plan** or **Keep current plan**.
- **Make a new plan:** different dishes, shown as a preview.
- **Grocery list:** from today to Sunday, everyone's plans added up (or "Just me"), grouped by aisle (vegetables, pulses, dairy, …); dishes contribute their recipe ingredients scaled to the servings, simple foods themselves.

### Round two: chat, your own dishes, fuller meals, a calmer page

- **Fuller, more varied meals:** lunch is a protein dish (dal, beans, paneer, eggs, meat or fish) + a vegetable dish (sabzi) + roti or rice + raita or salad; dinner a protein dish + roti or rice, with a sabzi when there's room. Mains are told apart by their ingredients (pulses), diet and name. No dish appears more than twice a week (chapati and rice excepted); if few dishes fit, the least-used repeats. Portions shrink salad first, then the sabzi, then the main when a meal would overshoot.
- **Your own dishes** (`backend/core/nutrition/dishes.py`): **Add a dish** (from "About this plan", a swap search or the chat). The AI drafts a typical home recipe from the name (raw grams for the whole recipe, servings, role); each ingredient is matched to USDA, first from a fixed list of about 55 everyday Indian ingredients (atta, besan, dals, ghee, paneer → queso fresco as the closest match, …), the rest searched and picked by the AI. You check and edit the grams, matches (search the ingredient database), servings and role, with the numbers worked out live; then **Save dish**. Saved in `foods` for the household (`source` custom); used by new plans (always on the candidate lists), swaps and the chat. Only whoever added a dish removes it.
- **Swaps:** any dish in a meal, not just the main one: 12 suggestions of the same kind (a dal for a dal, a sabzi for a sabzi, rice for chapati), or **search all dishes** (spelling variants understood: chole = chana = channa, dal = daal, paratha = parantha, …; dishes named that way first, then dishes containing it). Not found: **Add it as a new dish**.
- **Ask for a change** (chat, `backend/core/nutrition/chat.py`): type a request in your own words. The AI turns it into changes: a named dish in a meal ("aloo paratha for Sunday breakfast"), eating out, or the rest of the week made again with a request and foods to leave out ("no chicken this week, more eggs"). The rules apply them and the result is a **preview** to use or keep, as with every change. Dishes not in the database are offered to add. When nothing could be changed, the reply says so (the AI's own words are only kept when changes were made). The week's chat is kept (your own only). If the AI can't be reached: "try again in a minute".
- **Layout:** one day at a time: a day strip, one summary line (calories planned / target, then protein, carbs, fat; tap for the reasons and vitamins and minerals), then each meal as one row (tap for portions, what each dish is made of, swaps and eating out). **🛒 Groceries**, **💬 Ask** and **Add a dish** open as overlays; the rationale and "Make a new plan" sit under "About this plan".

Next: an agentic chat with meaning-based dish search ([roadmap](../roadmap.md#m7--nutrition)).

Not yet: matching food logs (part 2), a cheat meal from the [Workout Plan](workout-plan.md) appearing here, and confirmed facts from [Personal Artifacts](personal-artifacts.md) (M9).
